editorial:
The Beast of Hollow Mountain (1956) is a US–Mexico western in which American rancher Jimmy Ryan (Guy Madison) finds a Tyrannosaurus living inside a mountain near a Mexican village. It was produced by Nassour Studios (Edward and William Nassour) with Películas Rodriguez, directed by Edward Nassour and Ismael Rodríguez, and released by United Artists in August 1956. The story grew from an original idea by Willis O'Brien, and Raúl Lavista is credited as composer. A creator would want it for the stop-motion dinosaur and the Mexican locations.

The rights trap is that nobody has confirmed the print is out of copyright. A 1956 film is public domain only if its notice was missing or its copyright was never renewed, and the renewal window ran through 1984. I could not check the catalog renewal volumes or the Copyright Office's online records, so the print stays undetermined. Internet Archive hosting is not evidence of status. Check the renewal record yourself before reusing the film commercially, and check the separate stop-motion, score and story elements.
faq: Is The Beast of Hollow Mountain in the public domain?

Not established. It was released in 1956, so its renewal window was 1984. I did not find a renewal record or confirm that none exists, so treat the print as undetermined. Search the Copyright Office public records and the 1984 Catalog of Copyright Entries renewal volume before relying on it.
Can I use the Internet Archive copy in my own project?
The Internet Archive lists the 1956 film, but hosting does not settle its copyright. Confirm the renewal status first. Any later edit, score or added titles on a given copy may carry its own rights.
